# Denosumab (Prolia) and Vertebral Fracture Risk in Osteoporosis: Evidence Summary

**Conclusion: Yes.** The evidence strongly supports that denosumab significantly reduces vertebral fracture risk in patients with osteoporosis, though this benefit carries an important caveat regarding treatment discontinuation.

## Primary Evidence

The pivotal **FREEDOM trial** (Fracture REduction Evaluation of Denosumab in Osteoporosis every 6 Months), a phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled study of approximately 7,800 postmenopausal women, established denosumab's efficacy. According to this trial's findings, denosumab reduced new radiographic vertebral fractures with a cumulative incidence of just 2.3%, compared to 7.2% in the placebo group—a risk ratio of 0.32 (p<0.001), representing roughly a **68% relative risk reduction** ([mdedge.com](https://www.mdedge.com/obgmanagement/article/65217/gynecology/osteoporosis/page/0/1); [reumatologiaclinica.org](https://www.reumatologiaclinica.org/en-denosumab-for-treatment-osteoporosis-a-articulo-S1699258X12001787)). This effect was consistent across risk levels, and the drug also reduced hip and nonvertebral fractures ([cfp.ca](https://www.cfp.ca/content/57/4/438)).

This benefit extends beyond Western populations: the **DIRECT trial** in Japanese postmenopausal women and men showed denosumab reduced vertebral fracture risk by 65.7% over 24 months, closely mirroring FREEDOM results.

## Important Caveat: Discontinuation Risk

A critical nuance in the evidence is the **rebound phenomenon** upon stopping denosumab. Post hoc analysis of the FREEDOM trial and its extension found that discontinuing denosumab is associated with rapid bone turnover increases and a heightened risk of multiple vertebral fractures, sometimes exceeding pretreatment risk ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5915244/)).

## Bottom Line

While continuously administered denosumab robustly reduces vertebral fracture risk, this benefit is contingent on sustained treatment or appropriate transition therapy upon discontinuation to avoid rebound fractures.
